title: Vibrantz: Two Queues for One Lifeboat

questions.prompt: What made Vibrantz's February 2026 deal the most talked-about restructuring of the year?
choices: S&P kept the company at D for the rest of 2026 while GoldenTree, Monarch and Oak Hill litigated over which of them held the first-out tranche
The company filed a prepackaged Chapter Eleven that handed the equity to its term-loan lenders, as had happened to the same sponsor's Air Methods in 2023
The nine percent noteholders were repaid at par from a two hundred million receivables facility while the term-loan lenders were left unpaid until 2030
Three funds approached separately got the safest new paper, while the other lenders saw terms only after signing an NDA and got paper worth about half of face
questions.explanation: The deal was run on two tracks: GoldenTree, Monarch and Oak Hill provided new money and got first-out paper; everyone else got second- and third-out paper after signing a non-disclosure agreement. There was no filing and no litigation on the public record.

questions.prompt: About how much new money did the three first-out funds put in, in millions of dollars, according to press accounts?
questions.explanation: Press reports put the first-out new money at about three hundred and fifty million dollars. The exact terms are not public.

questions.prompt: By December 2025, at what price in cents on the dollar was a lender fund (Barings) marking Vibrantz's first-lien term loan?
questions.explanation: The Barings mark of about fifty-five cents on a first-lien loan was the market saying even the secured lenders would not be paid in full, and it is the benchmark the episode compares the exchange prices to.

questions.prompt: Rank Vibrantz's post-exchange claims from most senior (paid first) to most junior.
items: First-out term loans (the new money and the three funds' exchanged paper)
questions.explanation: The revolver sits on rung one; the three tiers all share one first lien on rung two but are paid strictly in order, first-out, second-out, third-out; the sponsor's common sits on rung seven.

questions.prompt: All three tiers of the new term loans share the same first lien. If the collateral were sold for one billion dollars, what did the Host say happens?
choices: Each tier is paid the same cents on the dollar, because a shared lien means pari passu treatment across the tiers
The first-out is repaid in full, the second-out splits what is left, and the third-out receives nothing
The revolver and the third-out notes are paid first because their maturities in 2031 are the longest
The proceeds go to the second-out first, because at twelve to fourteen times leverage that is the fulcrum tranche
questions.explanation: The lien tells you what you can grab; the tier tells you who gets paid from it first. With about seven hundred and seventy million of first-out ahead, a billion of proceeds leaves only the remainder for the second-out.

questions.prompt: Why, according to the Host, did American Securities extend the debt out of court rather than file for Chapter Eleven?
choices: A filing would have triggered the two hundred million receivables facility and forced the company to repay the revolver first
Its equity is out of the money and behaves like an option, which a filing would kill but an extension keeps alive for free
The three first-out funds refused to provide new money unless the company avoided a rating agency default
Out-of-court exchanges are exempt from the absolute priority rule, so the sponsor could keep a share of the reorganised equity
questions.explanation: Sponsor option value: equity that far underwater has value only while the company avoids a filing. Air Methods, the sponsor's previous case, filed and emerged owned by its lenders nine weeks later.

questions.prompt: Per hundred dollars of old term loan, what did a lender outside the first-out room receive in the exchange?
choices: About ninety-eight dollars of first-out paper plus a pro rata share of the three hundred and fifty million of new money, the same package the three funds took
About sixty-five dollars of second-out and twenty-six of third-out paper, worth about fifty dollars at the company's own prices
One hundred dollars of second-out paper priced at sixty-six, plus a small allocation of the four million of second-out notes
About eighty dollars of mostly third-out paper, worth about thirty-one dollars, in exchange for giving up the old lien
questions.explanation: Ninety-two dollars of new face for a hundred of old, but at the tax-form issue prices of sixty-six and twenty-seven it was worth about fifty. The first-out queue held about ninety-eight on the same original loan; the noteholders' package was worth about thirty-one.

questions.prompt: What does the desk call a lender who has signed an NDA to see a company's private information and therefore cannot trade the name until it is public?
questions.explanation: Going restricted. Here the NDA also barred lenders from talking to each other or challenging the deal before it closed, which the episode called using the restriction as a gag.

questions.prompt: The Host called the new-money tranche the out-of-court cousin of which in-court instrument?
choices: The DIP loan, whose priority a judge blesses rather than the votes of the existing lenders
A three sixty-three sale, whose price the court approves in place of a lender vote
A litigation trust, funded by the estate to pursue claims on behalf of unsecured creditors
A consent fee, paid in cash to lenders who vote for a covenant waiver before the filing
questions.explanation: Same economics, different referee: fresh cash in exchange for priority at the top of the structure. In Chapter Eleven the court approves it; out of court, the amendment vote does.

questions.prompt: Name the IRS form Vibrantz posted in April 2026 that lists every exchange tranche and its issue price.
questions.explanation: Form 8937, the report of organisational actions affecting basis of securities, is often the only public document listing the tranches of a private exchange, and its issue prices are the market's marks on the new paper.

questions.prompt: For debt that trades, what does the issue price on the tax form represent?
choices: The price at which the company will redeem the tranche at maturity, net of the discount lenders accepted in the exchange
The price the three first-out funds paid in cash for their allocation, which the tax rules then apply to every tranche
The rating agency's recovery estimate for the tranche converted into cents on the dollar, one for ninety to one hundred percent and six for zero to ten
The trading value of the new paper in the month around the exchange, which the company reports so holders can compute gains and losses
questions.explanation: Issue price is a tax term: for publicly traded debt it is the trading value around issuance. Ninety-eight, sixty-six, twenty-seven and twenty-four are therefore market marks published by the company itself.

questions.prompt: Using the Host's rough numbers (interest of roughly 250 to 290 million against earnings of roughly 220 to 280 million), about what was Vibrantz's interest coverage, in times?
questions.explanation: About one times: every dollar earned goes to interest. The inputs are inferred from public coupons and S&P's leverage multiple, since the company publishes no financials.

questions.prompt: In the Host's household analogy, which ratio did interest coverage correspond to?
choices: The mortgage balance divided by the household's annual salary
The household's salary divided by the annual mortgage payment
The house price divided by the mortgage balance outstanding
The annual mortgage payment divided by the mortgage balance
questions.explanation: Leverage is the mortgage divided by salary; coverage is salary divided by the payment. You can live with a big mortgage if the payment is small, and Vibrantz cannot.

questions.prompt: Reading S&P's recovery ratings and the issue prices, where did the Host place the fulcrum security?
choices: In the second-out tranche, rated triple-C-minus with a recovery rating of five and priced at sixty-six
In the third-out tranche, rated double-C with a recovery rating of six and priced at twenty-seven, where the option on a recovery sits
In the first-out tranche, rated B-minus with a recovery rating of one and priced at ninety-eight
In the sponsor's common equity, which was not diluted and still holds all of the upside
questions.explanation: Value covers the seven hundred and seventy million of first-out and runs out inside the one and a half billion of second-out. That is Moyer's fulcrum; the third-out is an option on a recovery and the equity an option behind that.

questions.prompt: Nobody missed a payment, yet S&P rated Vibrantz D on February the twentieth. Which two tests did the Host say the agency applies?
choices: Whether the company breached a financial covenant in its credit agreement, and whether the lenders waived that breach in return for a consent fee
Whether the new paper trades below eighty cents, and whether the sponsor contributed new equity
Whether the exchange was approved by a court, and whether more than ninety percent of holders participated
Whether holders received less than originally promised, and whether the company would have defaulted anyway without the exchange
questions.explanation: A distressed exchange is a default under the agencies' rules when both tests are met. S&P called the deal tantamount to default, rated it D on completion and re-rated the new structure two weeks later.

questions.prompt: Why did the two weeks between the D rating and the triple-C re-rating matter to the loan's holders?
choices: In a CLO's tests a defaulted loan counts at market value, about fifty cents, while a triple-C loan inside the allowed bucket counts at par
A CLO must sell any loan rated D within thirty days of the downgrade, so the holders would have been forced sellers of Vibrantz at about fifty cents
A defaulted loan cannot pay its coupon into the CLO's waterfall until the rating is restored, starving the equity slice
Fitch required CLOs holding Vibrantz to hold extra capital against it for as long as the D rating stood
questions.explanation: CLOs, a bank made of a spreadsheet, hold most of a loan like this. Their tests treat a defaulted loan at market value and a CCC loan at par, which is the criticism Rod Dubitsky made of the quick re-rating.

questions.prompt: According to Fitch, in what percentage of the US broadly syndicated loan CLOs it rates did Vibrantz appear in February 2026?
questions.explanation: Twenty-nine percent, making Vibrantz the most widely held defaulted issuer of the month.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the contract among lenders, usually holding a majority of a loan, to negotiate as a block and take no side deal?
questions.explanation: A cooperation agreement, or co-op, is the lenders' union. Scott Greenberg of Gibson Dunn predicts that aggressive sponsors will produce more of them in 2026.

questions.prompt: Which description of what the exchange did to Vibrantz's finances matches what the Host reported from S&P?
choices: It cut the debt quantum by about eleven percent and reduced cash interest through the new tiers, which is why S&P moved the outlook from negative to developing in March
It converted the third-out tranches to payment-in-kind so that free cash flow turns positive in 2026
It cancelled scheduled amortisation, pushed maturities to 2030 and 2031 and added cash, while cash interest rose and the debt quantum stayed largely unchanged
It replaced the floating-rate term loan with fixed nine percent notes, removing the rate exposure that broke the credit
questions.explanation: Runway, not repair. S&P's negative outlook names the triggers for redefault: continued cash burn, liquidity below uses, a skipped interest payment or another distressed exchange.

questions.prompt: In the trader's recap, who was left in the dust?
choices: The second-out term-loan holders, mostly CLOs, who ate the market's loss and were primed behind the new first-out tranche
The three first-out funds, whose new money was subordinated to the new revolver
The third-out noteholders at twenty-four cents, and any holdout sitting behind three billion of newly senior debt
American Securities, which lost control of the company to its lenders as it had at Air Methods
questions.explanation: Winners: the first-out three and, for now, the sponsor. Losers: the second-out holders. Left in the dust: the third-out noteholders and the holdouts, whose treatment under the amendment is not public.
